title: Social-Cognitive Theory (Bandura)
summary: Bandura's social-cognitive theory: reciprocal determinism (person × behaviour × environment), observational learning/modelling, self-efficacy, and the Bobo doll experiment. Supplemented with academic enrichment — source PDFs do not cover Bandura directly.
objectives: Describe observational learning and its four processes.
Define self-efficacy and its behavioural effects.
revision: Bandura's social-cognitive theory: reciprocal determinism (person × behaviour × environment), observational learning/modelling, self-efficacy, Bobo doll experiment. Academic enrichment — not covered in Unit 07 source PDFs.
traps: Observational learning: attention → retention → reproduction → motivation.
Self-efficacy = belief in one's capability to succeed.

notes.t: Bandura's social-cognitive theory emphasises that people learn through observing others, and that cognition, behaviour and environment mutually influence each other. Note: this topic is academic enrichment; the Unit 07 source PDFs do not directly cover Bandura.
The bidirectional influence among person (cognition), behaviour and environment — each affects and is affected by the others.
Learning by observing the behaviour of a model and the consequences of that behaviour, without direct reinforcement.
A person's belief in their capability to organise and execute actions required to attain given outcomes.
Children who observed an adult model behaving aggressively toward a Bobo doll were more likely to imitate that aggression, demonstrating observational learning.

i: Four processes of observational learning: attention, retention, reproduction, motivation
Self-efficacy affects effort, persistence and resilience
Vicarious reinforcement: learning from others' rewards/punishments

notes.t: UGC NET may contrast Bandura's social-cognitive view with Freud's psychoanalytic and trait approaches.

mnemonics.title: ROSE
mnemonics.text: R — reciprocal determinism, O — observational learning, S — self-efficacy, E — Bobo doll experiment

flashcards.a: Learning by watching a model and its consequences.
